ei.title: When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

fullPassage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging consumption, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.

det.korean: 고객들이 패스트푸드를 자주 먹지 않도록 만류했다(discouraged). encouraged(장려했다)는 부적절.

det.analysis: ✅ ④persuade: 설득하다. ❌ ①purchase(구매하다). ❌ ②produce(생산하다). ❌ ③prohibit(금지하다).
det.tip: persuade: 설득하다. persuade someone to do = ~에게 ~하도록 설득하다.

questions.passage: This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This (convention) marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: convention(명사) → conventional(형용사) → unconventional(반대 형용사). 명사 strategy를 수식하는 형용사 자리이고, 글의 맥락상 '관습에 얽매이지 않는' 의미.
det.tip: convention(관습, 명사) → conventional(관습적인, 형용사) → unconventional(파격적인). un- 접두사.

questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 문맥에 맞게 어형 변환하여 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: success(명사) → successful(형용사) → successfully(부사). have used를 수식하는 부사 자리.
det.tip: success(성공, 명사) → successful(성공적인, 형용사) → successfully(성공적으로, 부사). 동사 수식 = 부사.

questions.passage:
When Not Selling Becomes the Best Sell

Have you ever come across an advertisement that actually encourages customers not to buy a product? It does not seem to make sense, but there are instances where companies have successfully used this somewhat odd approach. For example, there was a fast-food company that was concerned about public criticism on negative health effects due to the high fat content of fast food. Instead of trying to dispute the public criticism and claim their food was healthy, the company tried something different. They discouraged customers from eating fast food, like hamburgers, too often. Unexpectedly, this approach had an interesting effect. The company gained a positive image as being socially responsible, attracting more customers. This approach was also successful in the world of fashion. There was a rising concern about buying clothes and throwing them away quickly. This type of fast fashion trend has a destructive impact on the environment because excessive production of clothes produces a massive amount of waste. Surprisingly, one fashion company started to persuade people not to buy their clothes. They argued that people should consume less and far more slowly. This unconventional marketing strategy not only raised awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion on the environment, but also increased the company's sales. People thought that this brand really cared about the environment, and they started to buy more of this company's products. To sum up, both of these companies positioned themselves as responsible brands by discouraging ____, which ultimately captured the attention and appreciation of a growing audience.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis: ✅ ①consumption: 소비. discouraging consumption = 소비를 억제하다. ❌ ④competition(경쟁): 맥락 불일치. ❌ ②cooperation(협력): 무관. ❌ ③communication(소통): 무관.
det.tip: consumption: 소비. discourage consumption = 소비를 억제하다. 글의 핵심 전략.

det.korean: 이 브랜드가 정말로 환경을 신경 썼다고 사람들은 생각했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②cared: care about = ~을 신경 쓰다, 관심을 갖다. ❌ ①complained(불평하다): 부정적 뉘앙스. ❌ ③forgot(잊다): 반대. ❌ ④worried(걱정하다): care가 원문.
det.tip: care about: ~에 관심을 갖다, 신경 쓰다. 브랜드가 환경에 진심이라는 신뢰감.
